eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket heavily favors 20°C (91.5% implied probability) for Milan's highest temperature on May 12 at the Malpensa International Airport station, driven by ARPA Lombardia's latest forecast of sunny conditions with strong northerly winds—up to 60 km/h gusts—limiting daytime heating after yesterday's rain and hail. This positions below the May climatological average of 22°C due to persistent post-frontal stability. Realistic challenges include enhanced solar insolation if winds weaken or unexpected subsidence boosting to 21°C, with hourly station data providing final clarity by evening.

eventMetadata.context_description: PAGASA's latest 5-day outlook for Port Area, Metro Manila, projects a high of 34°C on May 14 under partly cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers possible (20% chance), anchoring trader sentiment in the mid-30s Celsius range amid May's peak dry-season heat. Close probabilities across 33–37°C reflect inherent forecast uncertainty from variable afternoon cloud cover, sea breeze timing, and urban heat island amplification, which have caused recent actual highs—like 35°C on May 12—to exceed guidance by 1–2°C. Historical May averages hover near 33–34°C, with extremes up to 38.5°C recorded on this date in 1987; upcoming 5 a.m. advisories and WRF model runs tomorrow could shift odds based on refined solar insolation and humidity trends.
